30 An electrical conductor has a resistance of 5.6 kΩ. A potential difference (p.d.) of 9.0 V is applied
across its ends.
How many electrons pass a point in the conductor in one minute?
A
6.0 × 1020
B
1.0 × 1019
C
6.0 × 1017
D
1.0 × 1016

hints: Notice the given $5.6\text{ k}\Omega$, $9.0\text{ V}$ and time of one minute, so first convert resistance to $5600\text{ }\Omega$ and time to $60\text{ s}$.
Connect current to these values with $I=V/R$, then connect current to total charge with $Q=It$.
Connect total charge to electron count with $Q=Ne$, using $e=1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, and check whether you multiplied by $60$ and divided by $10^{-19}$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $R=5.6\text{ k}\Omega = 5600\text{ }\Omega$, $V=9.0\text{ V}$ and $t=1\text{ minute}=60\text{ s}$.
Use Ohm's law to find the current: $I=V/R$.
Find the charge passing in one minute: $Q=It \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 \approx 0.0964\text{ C}$.
Use quantisation of charge $Q=Ne$ with $e=1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$: $N=Q/e$.
Substitute: $N \approx 0.0964/(1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \approx 6.0 \times 10^{17}$ electrons. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too large by a factor of 1000. It results if $5.6\text{ k}\Omega$ is used as $5.6\text{ }\Omega$ in $I=V/R$.

B.explanation: Too large by more than a factor of 10. It does not follow from $Q=It$ with $t=60\text{ s}$ and $N=Q/e$.

C.explanation: Gives $I \approx 1.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}$, $Q \approx 0.096\text{ C}$ in $60\text{ s}$, so $N=Q/e \approx 6.0 \times 10^{17}$.

D.explanation: Too small by a factor of 60. It is the number for $t=1\text{ s}$ instead of one minute of $60\text{ s$.
